oldValue: Charisma and race can adjust effective comeliness.
Extreme scores have special effects; consult the full table before applying them.
newValue: Roll 3d6 for base comeliness after the first six abilities. Charisma modifiers: below 3 −8; 3 −5; 4–5 −3; 6–8 −1; 9–12 0; 13–15 +1; 16–17 +2; 18 +3; above 18 +5. Later gains or losses of charisma adjust comeliness point for point.

Racial adjustment applies to reactions from other races: half-orc −3; dwarf or gnome −1; halfling or human 0; half-elf or sylvan elf +1; gray or high elf +2. Treat each starred pair as the same race for this purpose.

The following reaction bands concern creatures of human sort. At −16 or below, viewers recoil, flee or may attack; if viewer and subject are both evil, treat the score as positive. At −15 to −9, viewers show disgust and hostility; if all are evil, the negative score can be regarded as positive. At −8 to 0, viewers feel aversion and may become openly hostile.

At 1–6, viewers tend toward unease; enough conversation can let charisma offset it. At 7–9, the initial reaction is negative but high charisma can quickly overcome it. At 10–13, appearance has no effect on the viewer.
At 14–17, initial reaction improves by a percentage equal to the score; members of the opposite sex are affected as by fascination unless their Wisdom exceeds half the score.

At 18–21, initial reaction improves by 150% of the score. Opposite-sex viewers are affected as by fascination unless Wisdom exceeds two-thirds the score; same-sex viewers are similarly affected unless Wisdom is at least half the score. Harsh rejection can cause the rejected individual to react as if the subject had negative comeliness equal to half the positive score.

At 22–25, the reaction adjustment is twice the score. Fascination affects those with Wisdom less than two-thirds of the score; a consciously sought opposite-sex individual is fascinated unless Wisdom is 18 or higher. Harsh rejection has the same effect as in the 18–21 band.

At 26–30, reserved for unusual extraplanar demigods or deities, the reaction adjustment is twice the score. Fascination applies except to those with Wisdom at least 75% of the score, and Wisdom 19 or higher always permits a saving throw. A consciously sought opposite-sex individual is affected unless Wisdom is 20 or higher.

Fascination allows a saving throw versus spell; nonmagical comeliness fascination is not removed by dispel magic or antimagic. A fascinated creature follows an order if 3d6 does not exceed the subject’s comeliness: add 1 to the roll for requests against its interest, up to +6 or more for hazardous requests; a higher roll breaks fascination. Treatment during fascination affects subsequent reaction.

Comeliness is temporary as a reaction factor: once the subject is known, use charisma. Fascination does not prevent fighting or spellcasting or make the subject a puppet. Change self and alter self adjust comeliness by at most 1 point; an illusion of a high-comeliness creature works for one round; polymorph changes it by 2 points; shapechange gives the final form’s full effect.

Attack rates use the specialization table rather than the ordinary rate where applicable.

newValue: Only fighters and rangers may specialize, choosing at character creation. Specialization costs two proficiency slots; a non-crossbow bow requires one additional slot. The weapon must be a specific type.
Melee specialization grants +1 to hit and +2 damage in addition to applicable Strength and magic bonuses. Other missile weapons also grant +1 to hit and +2 damage.

Bow point blank is 6–30 feet: +2 to hit and damage and double damage on a hit; the source gives 6–16 damage for a nonmagical arrow, plus applicable Strength or magic bonuses. At short range, beginning at 30 feet up to the lower limit of medium range, the specialist gains +1 to hit and damage. A nocked and drawn bow with target in sight may fire before initiative.

Crossbow point blank is 6–60 feet: +2 to hit and damage and double damage, with a 6–12 nonmagical light-crossbow example excluding Strength or magic bonuses. At short range gain +1 to hit and damage; at medium gain +1 to hit with no specialization damage bonus. A cocked and aimed crossbow with target in range gains a shot before initiative.

The table supersedes ordinary fighter/ranger attacks for the specialized weapon.

Double specialization costs another proficiency slot when a character qualifies for a new weapon, and must be in the weapon already specialized in. Only melee weapons qualify, excluding pole arms and the two-handed sword; it gives +3 to hit and +3 damage with that weapon.
